subject: Private offer: burst-credit policy + seller-fee amortization questions
messages:
From: Katie Long <katie.long@dataharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@dataharbor.com, Paul Yang <paul.yang@dataharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace private offer — need clarification on burst credits & seller fee amortization

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for walking us through the Redwood private offer structure yesterday. Procurement reviewed the draft term sheet and we have two operational asks before we route to legal:

1) Burst credits / overage guardrail: our platform usage spikes by ~35% for seasonal jobs. We need a clear mechanic for short-term bursts so we don’t immediately incur large overage invoices. Is there a way to bake in a "burst credit pool" (one-time token credit that sits aside for the first N bursts) or a temporary multiplier discount for overage tokens in month-of-burst?

2) Seller fee amortization: our reseller (BrightBridge) wants the partner/seller fee to be amortized across the committed term rather than taken as an upfront deduction. Practically that means listprice * partner-commission = charged monthly instead of netting at invoice time. Can Redwood support an amortized seller fee path (and will that affect Marketplace listing fee/HubSpot reporting)?

I attached our RFP and a clean copy of the pricing workbook. We tried to map your SKU families to ours — there are some mismatches in the reserved capacity vs metered SKU mapping.

High-level ask: concrete wording and an operational path we can include in the PO that satisfies both procurement and our reseller. Can you loop in billing/ops and confirm?

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Long
Director, Procurement
DataHarbor

Attachments: DataHarbor_RFP_v3.pdf (pdf), DH_pricing_workbook_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — need clarification on burst credits & seller fee amortization

Katie — thanks for the clear asks and the workbook, that helps. Quick answers and next steps below.

Burst credits: yes — we can implement a one-time burst-credit pool that applies to token overages for 3 months post-PO effective date. Operationally we treat it as a prepaid credit line (not a discount) that is consumed before regular overage rates. It shows up on the invoice as a separate line item: "Burst credit applied - DH PO".

Two constraints:
- Credits are consumed FIFO and are attached to the account (not transferable across BrightBridge sub-accounts).
- Bursts larger than 5x baseline in a month will be billed at an elevated overage rate (to avoid gaming).

Seller fee amortization: we support amortization but it depends on the invoicing path. Three options:
A) Redwood invoices DataHarbor net of seller fee each month (we amortize internally; seller receives partner payout separately).
B) Redwood invoices gross; we generate a monthly partner-fee line and pass partner payout via BrightBridge's reseller invoicing.
C) BrightBridge handles seller fee outside Redwood (preferred by some resellers).

Option B is the cleanest for accounting: Redwood can emit gross invoices with a partner-fee line and amortize that fee monthly across the committed term. That preserves HubSpot/Marketplace reporting and avoids a large upfront netting. I'll bring Marissa and Mina in for ops/finance confirmation.

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm operational feasibility for a 3-month burst credit pool and draft the invoice line wording we should put in the PO? Mina — please confirm if amortization via gross invoice (Option B) works for revenue recognition and whether it needs any contract-side language.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — operational notes on burst credits & seller fee amortization

Thanks Ben and Katie — operational notes below so procurement can include precise wording in the PO.

Burst credit pool (our implementation detail):
- Term: applies for first 90 days after PO effective date.
- Amount: one-off credit amount (we will reference DH PO # in invoice).
- Invoice treatment: credit appears as separate line item; overage consumption reduces the credit balance until exhausted.
- Safety valve: if cumulative bursts > 500% of committed baseline within 90 days we will flag and require an account review (possible rate adjustment or temporary hard cap).

Suggested PO language (short):
"Redwood will provide a one-time \"Burst Credit Pool\" of [USD amount] to be applied against token overages for 90 days following the Effective Date. Burst credits will be applied prior to regular overage billing and will be shown as a separate invoice line item referencing the Purchase Order number. Overages in excess of 5x baseline in any single month may be billed at an elevated overage rate after notice to Customer."

Seller fee amortization (finance note):
- We can issue gross invoices with a monthly Partner Fee line that amortizes the seller/reseller fee over the committed term. Revenue recognition will follow our standard rules (we'll provide the amortization schedule).
- Tax/VAT: for EU/UK customers the seller fee treatment can change VAT handling. For DataHarbor (US) we will not change VAT but will provide a clear gross/gross-net breakdown on the invoice.
- BrightBridge routing: if BrightBridge is the reseller, we need the reseller Hub ID to wire partner payouts correctly.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Operations
Redwood Inference
